The sink is an assertion diagnostic in the cfg(test)-only authorization dispatcher fixture. It formats local synthetic operation results and roles, not a production logger or account credential. The reviewed test calls use fixed fixture participants and messages. Since f514deb9 the printed result is the dispatcher's Result<(), RoomError>, and the analysis also traces a closure and session.media_session_id at src/room/manager/moderation_ops.rs:495 into it, beside the two room-join password values and verify_room_password calls in src/room/manager/membership.rs. The Ok payload is unit and every refusal those paths raise carries fixed text: verify_room_password consumes the supplied password and refuses with the fixed Forbidden("Incorrect room password"); the media session id only selects the session to remove, its absence becomes the fixed NotFound("Target participant not found") refusal, and a media cleanup failure is logged there, not returned; neither the supplied room password nor the media session id is bound into any query on these paths, so a database error on them cannot echo either value. Neither the password nor a session identifier can reach the printed text.

The cfg(test) SensitiveValues.assert_absent assertion evaluates a boolean containment check and formats only the fixed label and surface strings. All 13 callsites pass literal surface names; labels are literals supplied directly or through fixed tuple arrays. Neither the sensitive value, its encodings nor the observed output is a formatting argument. The reported receiver-level flows do not represent a secret reaching this diagnostic.

The sensitive-name heuristic treats the entire local account Option and refresh receiver as account data; the reported sink is format!(self.origin) passed as the reqwest request URL. That value contains only the validated public loopback origin and fixed /api/auth/refresh path, without credentials, bearer token or cookie. The generator requires a plain literal loopback IPv4 endpoint for account workloads; the account helper module additionally rejects URL userinfo, query, fragment and paths other than /ws, disables redirects and proxies, and bounds requests. Separate fixture credentials are intentionally sent in body/header only to this disposable local server. This decision covers the reported public-URL taint in the owned experiment, not remote HTTP authentication. Since the workspace change the helper is the module file load_tests/src/account_session.rs and the identity binds that complete file, so any guard change there invalidates the approval.
